trust_decision.summary: Whether a state-changing HTTP request carries a valid session CSRF token is decided by django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware; at the pinned commit that middleware exists only inside the dead MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES tuple, which modern Django no longer reads, so the live MIDDLEWARE chain decides nothing and every HTML POST is accepted cross-site. One config site governs the whole HTML route surface.

landing_point.why: The advisory names a regression introduced by the Django migration, so the first look is at the middleware configuration; grep for 'csrf' lands on the live MIDDLEWARE tuple, which lists no CsrfViewMiddleware.

fix_sites.entry_point: the entire HTML route surface registered under settings.API_ONLY == '0' in mobsf/MobSF/urls.py:215 (e.g. /login/, /upload/, /delete_scan/, /suppress_by_rule/, /execute_adb/) — all of it is reached through one global middleware stack, so a single settings change covers every route
fix_sites.module_kind: settings/config (Django middleware chain; no handler code changed)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue CSRF is a browser-session concern only: the /api/v1/ views are already csrf_exempt and authenticate with an X-Mobsf-Api-Key/Authorization header no cross-site form can set, and the remaining state-changing GET helpers are download/navigation routes rather than the POST surface the middleware fix was about.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The key-authenticated REST API under /api/v1/ must stay csrf_exempt; an over-broad 'protect every view' fix that strips the decorators makes every CLI/CI client fail with 403. Separately, /generate_download/ is reached by plain <a href> GET links (mobsf/templates/static_analysis/android_binary_analysis.html:658), so forcing it to POST breaks the download buttons.

O6_input_shapes: AJAX POST carrying csrfmiddlewaretoken as a data field (mobsf/templates/general/home.html:127)
AJAX request carrying the X-CSRFToken header (mobsf/templates/general/tasks.html:84)
unsafe methods other than POST (PUT/PATCH/DELETE) are checked by the same middleware

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /generate_download/?hash=<md5>&file_type=java|smali writes a zip into DWD_DIR with shutil.make_archive; no CSRF check applies to this route before or after the fix
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a GET, Django's CSRF middleware guards only unsafe methods, the handler only builds a download archive, and the UI reaches it with a plain anchor link, so converting it to POST is a behaviour change beyond the advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: mobsf/MobSF/views/home.py — 1 file / same package as the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /static_scan/<checksum> pulls the installed APK off the device and appends a recent-scan DB row via add_to_recent_scan; no CSRF check applies
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a GET navigation route in a different package with no @require_http_methods, and the advisory's fix was a middleware restore, so a solver can argue GET CSRF was never covered by it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: mobsf/DynamicAnalyzer/views/android/dynamic_analyzer.py — 3 files / 2 packages from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: have RestApiAuthMiddleware set request._dont_enforce_csrf_checks (or short-circuit) for a path prefix, silently exempting a whole route family from CSRF
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MobSF already ships its own Django middleware in this package for API auth, so centralising an exemption there is the natural place a maintainer would write it and it would read as a performance shortcut.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second stale MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES-style tuple in an environment/deployment settings overlay that keeps the real CSRF middleware out of the live chain
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project genuinely carried the dead tuple forward from its pre-Django-2 configuration; keeping a compat copy in a deployment settings module is exactly the mistake that produced this advisory.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an over-broad @csrf_exempt on saml_acs (or on the login view) added to keep the IdP POST working
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The SAML ACS receives a cross-origin POST with no token by design, so enabling the middleware forces a maintainer to write an exemption there; writing it one decorator too wide re-opens the hole.

O9_family: CWE-352 Cross-Site Request Forgery — protection disabled by configuration (CSRF middleware stranded in a dead settings tuple)

O10_build.toolchain: Poetry; Python >=3.12; Django 6.0.3 (poetry.lock:823); tox envs py312/py313; manage.py test
O10_build.project_tests: mobsf/StaticAnalyzer/tests.py:589 StaticAnalyzerAndAPI (django.test.TestCase) uses django.test.Client, which disables CSRF enforcement by default, so it does not cover this area; there are no CSRF-specific tests and the fix diff adds none.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add CsrfViewMiddleware to MIDDLEWARE and stop there, or — after seeing UI 403s — sprinkle @csrf_exempt across views, instead of also moving the state-changing GET routes onto POST and keeping the API/SSO exemptions narrow.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit 62563ca bundles four advisories; only the mobsf/MobSF/settings.py hunk belongs to this CSRF advisory — the other eight source files are the SSRF, zip-bomb, path-traversal and command-injection fixes and were not pursued.

The same dead-tuple root cause also kept SecurityMiddleware and XFrameOptionsMiddleware (restored by the fix) plus WhiteNoise/Common/Ratelimit middleware (not restored) out of the live chain; rate limiting and clickjacking are outside this advisory's protection and were not pursued.
